card.title: KM PRINZ EUGEN

card.flavorText: The Prinz Eugen was a German heavy cruiser of the Admiral Hipper class which served in the Kriegsmarine during WWII. She was named after Prince Eugene of Savoy, a notable 18th-century general of the Austrian Habsburg dynasty. In May 1941, Prinz Eugen participated in Operation Rheinübung, accompanying the battleship Bismarck in an attempt to disrupt Allied shipping in the Atlantic. During the Battle of the Denmark Strait on 24 May, the two ships engaged British forces, resulting in the sinking of HMS Hood and damage to HMS Prince of Wales. In 1942, she took part in Operation Cerberus, a daring dash through the English Channel alongside Scharnhorst and Gneisenau to return to Germany. After that, she was deployed to Norway but suffered significant damage from a torpedo attack by the British submarine HMS Trident, necessitating extensive repairs. Later in the war, Prinz Eugen provided artillery support on the Eastern Front, assisting German forces during their retreat. After Germany's surrender in May 1945, the ship was handed over to the British as a war prize, and then transferred to the US Navy. She was renamed USS Prinz Eugen (IX-300) and subjected to nuclear testing during Operation Crossroads at Bikini Atoll. She survived the blasts, and was eventually towed to Kwajalein Atoll where she capsized and sank in December 1946. Today, parts of her wreck remain visible above the water.
